delay.note: the existing figure is a sum of cascaded time constants, not a propagation delay; it is an order-of-magnitude comparison only

system_delay.equation: t_stop = t_CT/rectifier/filter + t_cmp + t_common_logic + max(t_primary, t_SR)
system_delay.common_logic_note: the D0 CD4013 latch and its gating are not modelled here, so every total below is a floor, not a worst case

sr_branch_terms.excluded_input_rc_reason: the 10 us RC is the validation board's front end, not the main board's fault path

system_delay.note: the 121x module figure is a detection-only comparison; against the whole machine the comparator change is worth the ratio below, because the REG crowbar sets the stop time

supply.shutdown_logic: SHDN low enables; within 0.9 V of V+ disables
supply.loss_of_5v: reference and comparator dead; R6 holds Q1 off, so FAST_TRIP is released -- no false trip, but no fast protection either
supply.minimum_reference_current: UNVERIFIED - the LM4040D25IDBZR minimum operating current is not in this repository

d0_connection: J1.1 V5 -> D0 V5 (bench 5 V rail)
J1.3 OCD -> D0 R8/OCD node (the burden, before R9)
J1.4 FAST_TRIP -> D0 FAST_TRIP (R15/TP8); both drivers are open drain

observations.finding: The LM393 is not the bottleneck: the three filters in front of it total ~127.6 us of time constants.
The module trips at 76.6 A peak (7.66 V burden) and releases at 73.4 A; the nominal divider crossing is 75.0 A.
observations.evidence: divider arithmetic against the references/datasheets/tlv3501.txt reference and the project CT transfer 0.1 V/A

observations.finding: Total module delay is ~1.06 us using the 12 ns over-temperature comparator number, about 121x faster than the existing filtered path.
observations.evidence: references/datasheets/tlv3501.txt switching characteristics, overdrive 5 mV, -40 to +125 C

observations.finding: That 121x is detection only. With the SR board's shutdown branch added, the whole-machine stop goes from ~144.8 us to ~16.9 us -- 8.5x -- because the sr branch sets it. D0's latch is not modelled, so both are floors.

The input pin stays inside the common-mode range up to 144 A peak. Above that the comparator is out of range but still inside its absolute maximum, so it is already tripped and the output state no longer matters.
observations.evidence: references/datasheets/tlv3501.txt common-mode range (V-)-0.2 V to (V+)-0.2 V, absolute maximum (V-)-0.3 V to (V+)+0.3 V

observations.finding: The threshold sits above the 73.68 A peak of the frozen short-circuit deck, so that case is left to the controller's own overcurrent. The module is aimed at the 84-101 A severe faults.
observations.evidence: design/v3/power_priority: lr_design.json PHYSICAL_PEAKS and the hotfault prefixes

observations.finding: SHDN tied high would disable the comparator; it is tied to PGND through R8.
observations.evidence: references/datasheets/tlv3501.txt shutdown section: high (within 0.9 V of V+) disables, more than 1.7 V below V+ enables

observations.finding: The module does not latch; the CD4013 on D0 does. Used standalone, the output follows the current.
observations.evidence: D0 FAST_TRIP net and CD4013 unit 4

limits: module only; the CT, rectifier and burden stay on D0
the system stop is NOT set by this comparator: the SR branch waits for REG to fall through UVLO, so the whole-machine floor is quoted in system_delay
D0's CD4013 latch propagation is not modelled, so system_delay totals are floors
no latch, no isolation, no reverse-supply protection beyond D2
the LM4040D25IDBZR minimum operating current is unverified, so the low-supply corner is not characterised
a clean ERC only says the drawing agrees with itself
